chapter: New Orleans ballrooms and Tony Almerico
title: Stage hazards and the Cab Calloway band fight story
summary: Talk of keeping the stage clear for dancers leads Allen to the famous story of Dizzy Gillespie stabbing Cab Calloway, and Jones mentions Danny Barker.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Well if you work with dancers that would be very important, to keep the stage clean.

Yeah. I mean, even if you ever worked with any dancers, and what it could do to them. And they could trip and fall, so naturally. That, I never have had the experience of seeing that happen, but I know if I'm emceeing something, and I see something on the stage, I'll kick it out of the way. I'll just, well, famous spitball fights have taken place in the Cab Calloway band, and caused a lot of trouble.
I've been on bands that had fights on stage, but not spitball fights.

Yeah, but, well I mean, the story's about Dizzy Gillespie, ended up stabbing Cab Calloway. Ended up what? Stabbing Cab Calloway. Danny Barker was in the band. Yeah, and he was about, you know, a half an inch or something. No damage or anything. But that's a famous story.
I saw Danny Barker on the street a couple of weeks ago. I hadn't seen him in a long time. Now he's a hell of a storyteller.
